description.text:
Warning! This protocol is EXPERIMENTAL and under active development.
It may change at any time, including in backward-incompatible ways,
without incrementing the interface major version and without prior
notice. No compatibility guarantees of any kind are provided. Clients
and compositors must track the upstream definition in treeland-protocols
and must not rely on the current interface names, requests, events, or
semantics remaining stable across releases.

This protocol fine-tunes the compositor-drawn server-side decorations
(SSD) of the client's own toplevel windows: corner radius, shadow,
border, and titlebar visibility.

It is not standalone: the client must first negotiate SSD for the
surface via xdg-decoration. The compositor applies these requests
according to its own policy; in particular it may silently ignore a
set_* request on a surface that has not negotiated SSD, or clamp an
out-of-range value to a supported bound instead of raising an error.

This enables a "half-CSD, half-SSD" configuration: keep the
compositor's border, corners and shadow while hiding its titlebar
(set_titlebar_mode(hide)) and drawing a custom one.

Each property is opt-in: if a set_* request is never sent, the
compositor applies its own default for that window's SSD. Sending a
request takes ownership of that property for the lifetime of the
context.

The terms "must", "must not", "should", and "may" in this document are
to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119.

A global that creates per-surface SSD customization contexts.

Each surface may have at most one active decoration context.
Attempting to create a second context for the same surface while
one is already alive is a protocol error (already_used).
description.summary: factory for per-window SSD customization contexts

description.text:
Destroy the treeland_decoration_manager_v1 object.
Existing treeland_decoration_context_v1 objects
created through this manager are not affected and must be
destroyed separately by the client.

Create a treeland_decoration_context_v1 for the given
surface. The surface must be owned by the requesting client;
passing a surface owned by another client raises the
invalid_surface protocol error.

The surface should hold a toplevel role (xdg_toplevel). The
context itself may be created before SSD is negotiated; until
SSD is negotiated via xdg-decoration, set_* requests on the
context have no effect and are silently ignored by the
compositor.

Creating a second context for the same surface while one is
already alive is a protocol error (already_used).
description.summary: create a decoration context for a surface

args.name: id
args.summary: new decoration context for the given surface

args.name: surface
args.summary: surface to decorate; must be owned by this client

description.text: Error codes sent as protocol errors via wl_display.error.

entries.name: already_used
entries.summary: a decoration context already exists for this surface

entries.name: invalid_surface
entries.summary: the surface is not owned by the requesting client

description.text:
Controls the compositor-drawn server-side decorations for a single
surface. Created by
treeland_decoration_manager_v1.get_decoration_context.

All requests take effect immediately; there is no pending/commit
model. The compositor applies each change as soon as it processes
the request.

This object becomes inert when the underlying wl_surface is
destroyed; requests on an inert context are silently ignored.
The client should destroy this context before or immediately after
destroying the associated wl_surface.

Destroy the context. The compositor may revert any or all
customized properties to its default behavior after this
request.

Override the compositor's corner rounding for this surface.
Once set, the compositor no longer applies its global corner
radius to this window.

A value of 0 requests square corners. The compositor applies
this request according to its own policy and may clamp an
out-of-range value to a supported bound.

args.name: radius
args.summary: corner radius in pixels; 0 for square corners

description.text:
Override the compositor-drawn drop shadow for this surface.

When radius is 0 the shadow is disabled and all other
arguments are ignored. Color components are unsigned in
[0, 255]. The compositor applies this request according to its
own policy and may clamp an out-of-range radius to a supported
bound.

args.name: radius
args.summary: shadow blur radius in pixels; 0 to disable shadow

args.name: offset_x
args.summary: horizontal shadow offset in pixels; positive is right

args.name: offset_y
args.summary: vertical shadow offset in pixels; positive is down

description.text:
Override the compositor-drawn border for this surface.

When width is 0 the border is disabled and the color
arguments are ignored. Color components are unsigned in
[0, 255]. The compositor applies this request according to its
own policy and may clamp an out-of-range width to a supported
bound.

args.name: width
args.summary: border width in pixels; 0 to disable border

description.text:
Override whether the compositor draws a server-side titlebar
for this surface, per the titlebar_mode enum. A mode value
outside the titlebar_mode enum range is silently ignored; the
current titlebar visibility is kept.

Hiding the titlebar leaves the rest of the SSD (border,
corner radius, shadow) in effect; the client is then expected
to draw its own titlebar inside the window content.

Controls whether the compositor-drawn (server-side) titlebar
is visible, overriding the compositor's default. Hiding the
titlebar while keeping the rest of the SSD is what produces a
"half-CSD, half-SSD" configuration.

entries.name: show
entries.summary: show the compositor titlebar (the SSD default)

entries.name: hide
entries.summary: hide the compositor titlebar; the client is expected to draw its own titlebar inside the window content while keeping the rest of the SSD
